article_title: Aflac Japan Confirms Breach of 4.38 Million Customers and Agents After Attackers Accessed Its Policyholder Portal
summary: Substantively accurate breach report; all core facts and quotes verified verbatim against snapshots. Two inline citations credit true facts to the wrong (but still cited) outlet, filed as corrections.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece (463 words, within the 400-1200 News range). Sensible Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Context organization. Careful hedging ('may affect', 'likely', 'preliminary estimates') appropriate for a developing disclosure.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 source snapshots read from disk and decompressed. source-0.html.gz (BleepingComputer, Archive.org fallback, 200): CONFIRMS the U.S.-business-not-affected quote verbatim, the June 15-25 access window, June 30 announcement, and the prior-year breach with Scattered Spider indicators. source-1.html.gz (SecurityWeek, 200): CONFIRMS the 4.38 million customers-and-agents figure, the June 15/June 25 access-and-discovery window, the exposed-data-types quote verbatim, the ~230,000 premium-transfer-account figure, the no-credit-card statement, and the containment quote verbatim. Note: SecurityWeek's Aflac article does NOT contain the prior-breach/Scattered Spider content the article attributes to it. source-2.html.gz (The Record, 200): CONFIRMS the ~4.38 million policyholders figure, the ~230,000 premium-payment-account figure, the 'has not identified the attackers' quote verbatim, notification of Japanese police and cybersecurity authorities, the SEC 8-K filing, U.S.-business-not-affected, and the full Context cluster (Sapporo overseas subsidiaries, BlackField ransomware on Nidec's Taiwanese subsidiary with a $2 million demand, KDDI email-system access affecting five ISPs via a third-party software vulnerability). Note: The Record does NOT state Aflac engaged outside cybersecurity specialists (that detail is in SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Breach scale (4.38M), affected entity (Aflac Life Insurance Japan), access window (June 15-25, discovered June 25, announced June 30), exposed data types, ~230,000 financial-detail subset, and no-credit-card all confirmed. All four direct quotes are verbatim against their snapshots. Confirmed no unsupported 'two-week intrusion' duration claim remains anywhere in the body; the article states the June 15-25 window throughout (the only 'two weeks' reference in the sources is The Record describing the window of the multi-company disclosure cluster, not the Aflac intrusion). Two inline attributions credit true, cited facts to the wrong outlet (see corrections).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no exploit mechanics or attack step detail. Straight disclosure reporting.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Aflac coverage in the archive; genuinely new topic. Not a duplicate.
concerns: The prior-year Aflac breach and its Scattered Spider indicators are attributed inline to SecurityWeek, but that content appears in BleepingComputer's report, not in SecurityWeek's Aflac article. Fact is true and verifiable in a cited source; the outlet attribution is wrong. Filed as a correction.

The detail that Aflac 'engaged outside cybersecurity specialists to investigate' is attributed inline to The Record, but The Record reports the notifications and SEC filing without mentioning outside specialists; that detail is reported by SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer. Fact true and verifiable in cited sources; the outlet attribution is imprecise. Filed as a clarification.
recommendations: When a sentence blends facts drawn from more than one source, attribute each specific to the outlet that actually reported it rather than to a single trailing citation.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A solid, neutral, verbatim-accurate breach report whose only defects are two inline outlet-attribution slips on facts that are nonetheless true and present in cited sources. Neither touches the headline, summary, or lead. Publishes with a public corrections trail under APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.

content_preview.title: Aflac Japan Confirms Breach of 4.38 Million Customers and Agents After Attackers Accessed Its Policyholder Portal
content_preview.summary: Aflac Life Insurance Japan says attackers accessed its policyholder portal between June 15 and 25, exposing personal data on roughly 4.38 million customers and agents.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Aflac Life Insurance Japan has disclosed a data breach that may affect roughly 4.38 million people after attackers gained unauthorized access to its policyholder portal. According to [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/aflac-japan-data-breach-impacts-4-38-million/), the intrusion began on June 15, 2026, continued through June 25, and was discovered on the same day it ended.
